clinical_effect: Lower iron absorption when taken together
management: Separate by 2 hours if treating iron deficiency. A combined multivitamin is acceptable when iron status is not the target.

mechanism: Competition at DMT1 and ZIP transporters
management: Separate high-dose iron from zinc; a multivitamin with 18 mg iron and 11-15 mg zinc is a compromise.

mechanism: Induced metallothionein binds copper in enterocytes
management: Keep zinc below 40 mg/day or add 1-2 mg copper. A 25 mg zinc multi should contain copper.

mechanism: Inhibition of vitamin K-dependent carboxylase; platelet effects
management: Standard multivitamin doses (15-30 mg) are not a concern; high-dose E should be avoided.
Avoid supplemental retinol with prescription retinoids.

clinical_effect: Reduced levothyroxine absorption and worse TSH control
management: Separate by at least 4 hours.

mechanism: Reduced gastric acid prevents release of food-bound B12
management: Crystalline B12 in a multivitamin is absorbed without acid; monitor B12 if symptoms or long-term use.

mechanism: Reduced acid impairs ferric iron reduction
management: Use bisglycinate or take with vitamin C; treat deficiency with a dedicated course.
Periodic B12 measurement; a multivitamin may prevent but not treat deficiency.

clinical_effect: Reduced drug effect at high folate doses
management: Only with oncology guidance. Low-dose folic acid is used deliberately with low-dose methotrexate.

clinical_effect: False low TSH and false troponin results
management: Stop high-dose biotin 48-72 hours before tests; tell the laboratory.

mechanism: Ascorbate reduces ferric to ferrous iron
management: Beneficial in iron deficiency; a concern only in iron overload.

clinical_effect: Reduced anticoagulant effect in case reports
